newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Feb 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Feb 7.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The education minister is accused of trying to bribe members of parliament with 10 million baht in cash in an opposition ambush. Opposition MPs accused Sukhavich Rangsitpol yesterday of disgusting behaviour and demanded that he resign. If he refused, the prime minister should sack him, they said. They say the New Aspiration deputy leader handed out money in brown envelopes along with questionnaires on his reform plan. (BANGKOK POST, THE NATION)

- The powers of the courts and their administrators might be reduced drastically under proposals by the Constitution Drafting Committee. The panel, chaired by Anand Panyarachun, proposed a host of measures to prevent interference by administrators in trials, and said the people should have the right to criticise verdicts. The proposals are part of an attempt to introduce checks and balances into the judiciary which has guarded its powers jealously. (BANGKOK POST)

- A commuter express boat sank yesterday after colliding with a stationary sand-carrying barge on the Chao Phya River near a bridge. The passengers were forced to jump into the river after the collision, and the boat capsized after about a minute. Rescue workers and Navy divers soon arrived on the scene. They said around 40 passengers were pulled from the water during a four-hour operation. (THE NATION) (BANGKOK POST) + + + +

- Liberalising Thailand's aviation industry to allow carriers from all nations to land at Don Muang international airport is the latest idea of Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh. The "open skies" policy will be aimed mainly at boosting the country's tourism industry, once the country's top foreign exchange earner, he says, adding he hopes to turn the country into a shoppers' paradise. (BANGKOK POST)

- Incentives for two international exhibition centres costing a combined 3.36 billion baht will be on the agenda when Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh today chairs the Board of Investment for the first time. The companies planning the centres say they will strengthen Thailand's ability to host major meetings and exhibitions. Waiving of import tax on machinery used to build the projects will be a major talking point. (BANGKOK POST)

- Bangkok Bank executive chairman says if Bankers Trustee sues Somprasong Land for defaulting on its bond interest payments, his bank will follow suit to recover loans extended to the property company. He says his bank will consider the details before extending additional loans to the company. (THE NATION)
